hora.intro: Each ring is one day — twenty-four <1>horas</1> ruled in turn by the seven planets. The planet of the <2>first</2> hora after sunrise gives the day its name. sources.heading: Classical sources
sources.blurb: Calculations follow each treatise's traditional author and the Bikram Sambat year of the original text. The second line is the translator and editor's printed edition in BS.

bphs.credit: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra - Maharishi Parashara
bphs.edition: Translator & Editor Pandit Ganesh Dutt Pathak BS 2029 (preface); revised edition BS 2058. Savitri Thakur Prakashan, Rathyatra, Varanasi.
bphs.used: The rules and results of yogas formed in the birth chart.

yajnavalkya.credit: Yajnavalkya Smriti (Navagraha Shanti Prakarana) - Maharishi Yajnavalkya, traditionally dated about 1000 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
yajnavalkya.edition: Editor & Translator Umeshchandra Pandey BS 2024. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
yajnavalkya.used: The oldest classical basis for the Vedic Navagraha Shanti yajna. The first codification of the 9 grahas' samidha, adhidevata, pratyadhidevata, and the Vedic mantras and donation items for graha shanti.

bphs.credit: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra - Maharishi Parashara, traditionally dated about 1500 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
bphs.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Devchandra Jha BS 2028. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
bphs.used: The Navagraha Shanti chapter and the Arishtabhanga/dasha-phala sections. The rules for japa, tarpana, marjana, homa, and direction-wise graha worship to avert affliction during the dasha/antardasha of a maraka, debilitated, combust, or trishadayesha planet.

puranas.credit: Matsya Purana & Agni Purana - Maharishi Vedavyasa, traditionally dated about 3000 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
puranas.edition: Editor & Translator Dr. Ramprataap Tripathi Shastri BS 2046. Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, Prayag.
puranas.used: The Navagraha Mandala diagram, the 9 grahas' colors, their cardinal directions (Sun-East, Moon-NW, Mars-South, Mercury-North, Jupiter-NE, Venus-SE, Saturn-West, Rahu-SW, Ketu-upward), the bija mantras for homa, and the samidha-homa/shanti procedure for health and prosperity.

phaladeepika.edition: Editor & Commentator Dr. Sureshchandra Mishra BS 2063. Ranjan Publications, New Delhi.
phaladeepika.used: Chapter 26 (Graha Dravyani and Shanti Vidhana). The classical table of the 9 grahas' gems, metals, preferred grains/havishya, and the stotra recitation and donation to ease an afflicted planet's harm.

muhurtachintamani.credit: Muhurta Chintamani & Prayoga Ratna - Acharya Ram Daivajna / Narayana Bhatta, BS 1657
muhurtachintamani.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Kedardutt Joshi BS 2036. Motilal Banarsidass, Delhi.
muhurtachintamani.used: The practical procedure for the karmakanda and Navagraha homa — sankalpa, graha avahana, the Kali Yuga ×4 japa multiplier, the 10% dashamsha homa, tarpana, marjana, and the full purnahuti method.

uttarakalamrita.credit: Uttara Kalamrita - Kalidasa, traditionally dated about 57 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
uttarakalamrita.edition: Editor & Translator Jagannath Bhasin BS 2041. Ranjan Publications, New Delhi.
uttarakalamrita.used: The second Kanda (Shanti and ritual section). The principle of averting affliction through deity worship and japa-homa to appease planets during a malefic dasha, maraka influence, or transit affliction (Sade Sati, Dhaiya).

lalkitab.credit: Jyotish Lal Kitab - Pt. Rupchand Joshi / Pt. Benimadhav Goswami, BS 1996
lalkitab.edition: Editor B.M. Goswami BS 2065. Sagar Publications, New Delhi.
lalkitab.used: Simple sattvic remedies for graha rin (planetary debt) and graha dosha — bija mantra japa, setting the related item afloat in running water, burying it, and feeding animals/birds for immediate graha shanti.

vimshottari.credit: Vimshottari Dasha (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra) - Maharishi Parashara, traditionally dated about 1500 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
vimshottari.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Devchandra Jha BS 2028. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
vimshottari.used: The 120-year nakshatra cycle held as best suited to Kali Yuga. The 9-planet dasha year sequence (Sun 6, Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19, Mercury 17, Ketu 7, Venus 20 years). Dividing the 27 nakshatras from Krittika onward among the 9 planetary lords, deriving the starting dasha from the birth nakshatra's elapsed/remaining portion, and the proportional computation of Mahadasha, Antardasha, Pratyantardasha, Sookshma and Prana dasha, with results read through Kendra-Trikona (Yogakaraka), Trishadayesha and Maraka principles.

tribhagi.credit: Tribhagi Dasha (Keshava Paddhati & Jyotish Ratnamala) - Acharya Keshava Daivajna, BS 1653
tribhagi.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Ramyatna Ojha BS 1981. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Pustakalaya, Banaras.
tribhagi.used: Built on the same nakshatra basis as Vimshottari Dasha, but dividing the total 120-year span into 3 equal parts to form a 40-year cycle. Each planet's Mahadasha is exactly one-third of its Vimshottari duration (Sun 2y, Moon 3y4m, Mars 2y4m, Rahu 6y, Jupiter 5y4m, Saturn 6y4m, Mercury 5y8m, Ketu 2y4m, Venus 6y8m). Used specifically for finer prediction of Balarishta, short lifespan, and rapid/urgent life events.

yogini.credit: Yogini Dasha (Rudrayamala Tantra & Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra) - Maharishi Parashara / Tantra Shastra, traditionally dated about 1500 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
yogini.edition: Editor & Translator Dr. Sureshchandra Mishra BS 2065. Ranjan Publications, New Delhi.
yogini.used: The 8-Yogini dasha system based on a total 36-year cycle: Mangala (1y - lord Moon), Pingala (2y - lord Sun), Dhanya (3y - lord Jupiter), Bhramari (4y - lord Mars), Bhadrika (5y - lord Mercury), Ulka (6y - lord Saturn), Siddha (7y - lord Venus), and Sankata (8y - lord Rahu/Ketu). The classical method of finding the starting dasha from the remainder when the birth nakshatra number is divided by 8 (via 3 rounds), and reading direct, rapid results across the 36-year cycle.

bphs.credit: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra - Maharishi Parashara, traditionally dated about 1500 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
bphs.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Devchandra Jha BS 2028. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
bphs.used: The rule giving exaltation and Moolatrikona an equal 45 Shashtiamsha (Virupas) in Saptavargaja Bala, and Shadbala's 13 sub-divisions.

saravali.edition: Editor & 'Kantimati' Commentator Dr. Muralidhar Chaturvedi BS 2030. Motilal Banarsidass, Delhi.
saravali.used: The declination-preference rule for Ayana Bala — Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Venus strong in the northern declination; Moon and Saturn in the southern; and the special principle that Mercury is strong in both declinations.

jatakparijat.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Kapileshwar Shastri BS 2020. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
jatakparijat.used: The integrated mathematical evaluation of Shadbala that determines a planet's actual capacity to give results.

phaladeepika.edition: Editor & Commentator Dr. Sureshchandra Mishra BS 2063. Ranjan Publications, New Delhi.
phaladeepika.used: The three main components of Bhava Bala (Bhavadhipati Bala + Bhava Digbala + Bhava Drishti Bala), the use of the raw Shadbala total in Bhavadhipati Bala, and the rule for adding graduated Drishti Bala when a benefic or the house lord aspects or occupies the house.

brihatjataka.edition: Translator & Editor Swami Vijnanananda BS 1969. Allahabad Panini Office (No. 12).
brihatjataka.used: The rule that classifies Scorpio not as a water sign but solely as a 'Keeta' sign for Bhava Digbala, granting full 60-Virupa Digbala in the 7th house (West).

horasara.edition: Translator & Editor R. Santhanam BS 2041. Ranjan Publications, New Delhi.
horasara.used: The principle of splitting Sagittarius and Capricorn into two halves (0°-15° and 15°-30°) for Bhava Digbala, classifying each half as quadruped, human, or aquatic.

sripatipaddhati.edition: Translator & Editor V. Subrahmanya Sastri BS 1994. Sri Maruti Press, Bangalore.
sripatipaddhati.used: The mathematical formula for Bhava % (residential strength) — deriving result-capacity from the linear arc-distance ratio, treating the Bhava Madhya as 100% and the Bhava Sandhi as 0%.

jatakparijat.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Kapileshwar Shastri BS 2020. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
jatakparijat.used: The integrated mathematical evaluation of Bhava Bala that determines a house's actual capacity to give results.

bphs.credit: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra - Maharishi Parashara, traditionally dated about 1500 years before the Bikram Sambat epoch
bphs.edition: Editor & Translator Pandit Devchandra Jha BS 2028. Chaukhamba Sanskrit Series, Varanasi.
bphs.used: The 337-point Ashtakavarga (Trikona and Ekadhipatya Shodhana, the reduced Shodhya Pinda).

x.agni_absolute_tithi: Computed on the absolute tithi (śukla 1–15, kṛṣṇa 16–30) and vāra (Sun=1 … Sat=7).
x.agni_absolute_tithi_gloss: Count absolute tithis from śukla Pratipadā through kṛṣṇa Amāvasyā (30) — śukla 1–15, kṛṣṇa as 16–30. Add 1 plus the weekday number (Sun=1 … Sat=7) to the current tithi; divide by 4 and read the remainder.
x.agni_computation_basis: Agni-vāsa is computed from the tithi and vāra alone (our system's method, not a separate clause of the verse).
x.agni_computation_basis_gloss: The root verse itself derives Agni-vāsa from tithi + weekday alone — not a separate lagna/panchāṅga rule; the system uses only those two inputs.
x.agni_nitya_naimittika: For Nitya, Naimittika and Ābdika (annual) rites the Agni-vāsa check is not mandatory — it applies mainly to Kāmya (desire-driven) rites; major saṃskāras such as Upanayana/marriage also do not strictly require it.
x.agni_vasa_formula: Agni-vāsa — (tithi + vāra + 1) mod 4: a remainder of 0 or 3 puts Agni on Earth (Bhūmi), which is auspicious for havan.
x.agni_vasa_remainder: Remainder 1 puts Agni in Heaven (loss of life) and remainder 2 in Pātāla (loss of wealth) — both inauspicious.
x.annaprasan_birth_date: The exact date depends on the child's birth (the age window); the list shows the suitable days.
x.annaprasan_birth_date_gloss: «yugmamāse puṃso'yugme strīṇām» — even months for a boy, odd for a girl. Without the birth date the age window cannot be fixed.
x.annaprasan_daytime: Daytime — computed from sunrise to sunset (our system's method, not a separate clause of the verses).
x.annaprasan_daytime_gloss: Divine/saṃskāra rites are best in the forenoon (pūrvāhṇa); annaprāśana is not done at night. The system scans daytime (sunrise→sunset) — diurnal lagna search; pūrvāhṇa preference is the classical ideal.
x.annaprasan_guru_shukra_asta: Guru/Śukra asta — as a time-bound (nitya) saṃskāra, annaprāśana is not barred by the combustion of Jupiter or Venus.
x.annaprasan_janma_tara: Janma-tārā — the 1st, 10th, 19th and 25th tārā from the child's birth star are avoided (native-specific; not applied in the general list).
x.annaprasan_janma_tara_gloss: «janmārkṣa…» — own birth star (1), anujanma (10), trijanma (19) and mānasa (25) are barred for śubha work. Being native-specific, this is not applied in the general annaprāśana list — check the child's chart.
x.annaprasan_lagna_shuddhi: Lagna-śuddhi — benefics in kendra/trikoṇa/11th, malefics in the upachaya (3,6,11), the 10th empty, and the Moon not in the 1st/6th/8th — the classical ideal. The general calendar applies only the sign bar (Meṣa, Vṛśchika, Mīna), since full graha-lagna-śuddhi is native-specific.
x.annaprasan_month_age: Month/age — annaprāśana is governed by the child's age in lunar months after birth: even months (6,8,10,12) for a boy and odd months (5,7,9,11) for a girl. By tradition it is not performed in Adhik-māsa.
x.annaprasan_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — the 16 Mṛdu/Laghu/Chara/Sthira stars: Aśvinī, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśira, Punarvasu, Puṣya, U.Phalgunī, Hasta, Chitrā, Svātī, Anurādhā, U.Aṣāḍhā, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, U.Bhādrapada, Revatī.
x.annaprasan_nakshatra_gloss: «mṛdulaghucarasthiroḍuṣu» — Mṛdu (Mṛgaśira, Revatī, Chitrā, Anurādhā), Laghu/Kṣipra (Hasta, Aśvinī, Puṣya), Chara (Svātī, Punarvasu, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā), Sthira/Dhruva (Rohiṇī, the three Uttarās) — 16 stars in all.
x.annaprasan_safeguard_dosha: Safeguard doṣas — Vyatīpāta/Vaidhṛti yoga, Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) karaṇa, Dur-muhūrta (period only) and the eclipse day are removed (general muhūrta safeguards, not part of the cited verses).
x.annaprasan_safeguard_dosha_gloss: Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā (Viṣṭi) and Vaidhṛti are mahā-doṣa; the eclipse day and Dur-muhūrta period are also dropped as general muhūrta safeguards — not a separate clause of 5.16.
x.annaprasan_tithi: Tithi — the śubha tithis 2,3,5,7,10,13 and Pūrṇimā (śukla 15); Nanda (1,6,11), Rikta (4,9,14), Aṣṭamī (8), Dvādaśī (12) and Amāvasyā are barred.
x.annaprasan_tithi_gloss: The clause «riktānandāṣṭamīdarśadvādaśī…vinā» bars Riktā (4,9,14), Nanda (1,6,11), Aṣṭamī, Amāvasyā (darśa) and Dvādaśī — leaving 2,3,5,7,10,13 and Pūrṇimā as śubha.
x.annaprasan_vara: Vāra — Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri only (Sun, Tue, Sat barred).
x.annaprasan_vara_gloss: «arkakujārkibhirvinā» — excluding Arka (Sun), Kuja (Tue) and Arki (Sat); Mon, Wed, Thu and Fri are kept.
x.bratabandha_dosha: Doṣa — Dagdha, Śūnya, and Mars/Rāhu Latta days excluded.
x.bratabandha_dosha_gloss: Dagdha and Śūnya tithi defects, and days whose nakṣatra is struck by Mars/Rāhu Latta, are scrubbed under day-śuddhi.
x.bratabandha_dosha_source: Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi — Latta 6.19, Dagdha 1.8, Śūnya 1.10 (Śubhāśubha Prakaraṇa)
x.bratabandha_galagraha_gloss: Pratipadā, Caturthī, Saptamī, Aṣṭamī, Navamī, Trayodaśī, Caturdaśī and Pūrṇimā/Amāvasyā are barred as Galagraha defects for Upanayana.
x.bratabandha_graha: Graha — Jupiter & Venus must be udaya — neither combust nor bāla/vṛddha.
x.bratabandha_graha_gloss: When Jupiter or Venus is combust (asta), bāla (infant), vṛddha (old) or during malimluca, auspicious works are barred. Seven days before setting is vṛddha; seven days after rising is bāla — the medium rule.
x.bratabandha_karana_gloss: The word 'Bhadrā' in this verse denotes Viṣṭi karaṇa. The system treats the entire Viṣṭi karaṇa as barred.
x.bratabandha_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — per tradition mode below: Classical Upanayana (Kṣipra/Dhruva/Cara/Mṛdu + Maghā/Mūla), Nepali Panchāṅga (all except Bharaṇī/Kṛttikā/Maghā/Viśākhā/Jyeṣṭhā), or Liberal (Maghā also allowed).
x.bratabandha_nakshatra_gloss: The śāstra favours Hasta, Aśvinī, Puṣya, Mṛgaśira, Punarvasu, Maghā, the three Uttarās, Mūla and the cara stars — about 19 nakṣatras (Classical mode).
x.bratabandha_sankranti_eclipse: Sankrānti and eclipse (±3 days) barred; Dur-muhūrta skips only the affected period (not the whole day).
x.bratabandha_sankranti_eclipse_gloss: Time around Sankrānti and eclipse is rejected; Dur-muhūrta drops only the affected clock slice — not the whole day.
x.bratabandha_season: Season — Sun in an Uttarāyaṇa rāśi (Makara→Mithuna: Māgha–Āṣāḍha); Chaturmāsa & Adhik-māsa barred.
x.bratabandha_season_gloss: Auspicious in Māgha, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha when the Sun is in the northern course (Uttarāyaṇa). Adhik-māsa and Chaturmāsa are barred.
x.bratabandha_simhastha: Simhastha Guru — Jupiter in Siṃha (Leo) barred (toggle off if your community does not enforce it).
x.bratabandha_time_window_gloss: Upanayana must not be done in the afternoon — only forenoon or midday.
x.bratabandha_tithi_gloss: Daśamī, Ekādaśī, Dvādaśī, Dvitīyā, Tṛtīyā and Pañcamī are the favourable Upanayana tithis.
x.bratabandha_vara: Vāra — Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri only (Tuesday & Saturday barred).
x.bratabandha_vara_gloss: Per Pitāmaha (Brahmā), Tuesday is not auspicious; Saturday and Tuesday are krūra vāra — barred for Bratabandha. Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday are auspicious.
x.bratabandha_yoga_gloss: This verse lists several defects to avoid in auspicious work, including Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti. On that classical basis, our system applies Vyatīpāta and Vaidhṛti as yoga defects.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_dosha: Doṣa — Dur-muhūrta (period only), Sankrānti and the eclipse day excluded.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_graha: Graha — business opening is more lenient than other rites, so Guru/Śukra udaya is NOT required; daytime only (sunrise→sunset).
x.byaparik_pratisthan_graha_gloss: Verses 46–47 list rites barred when Guru/Śukra are combust or during Malmāsa — vivāha, bratabandha, building-start, pratiṣṭhā, etc. 'Vipaṇi' (opening a shop/trade) is not on that prohibition list, so Guru/Śukra udaya is not mandatory — more lenient than other saṃskāras. Timing is still limited to daytime (sunrise→sunset).
x.byaparik_pratisthan_lagna: Lagna — only fixed (sthira) and dual (dvisvabhāva) ascendants accepted; movable rejected.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_lagna_gloss: The verse explicitly bars 'ghaṭa' (Kumbha) lagna and its navāṃśa with 'vinā' (except). For lasting trade, fixed lagnas (Vṛṣabha, Siṃha, Vṛśchika) and dual ones (Mithuna, Kanyā, Dhanu, Mīna) are preferred; movable lagnas (Meṣa, Karkaṭa, Tulā, Makara) bring instability and are barred. The system accepts only sthira/dvisvabhāva.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_month: Month — all lunar months except Adhik-māsa (Chaturmāsa is allowed); the Sankrānti day is barred.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_month_gloss: Adhimāsa (Malmāsa) bars new trade and building rites. Around Sankrānti, 16 nāḍīs before and after (32 nāḍīs / the Sankrānti day) are barred for auspicious work — the system excludes the Sankrānti day itself.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — a fixed list of trade-favourable nakṣatras: Aśvinī, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśira, Punarvasu, Puṣya, U.Phalgunī, Hasta, Chitrā, Svātī, Anurādhā, U.Aṣāḍhā, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, U.Bhādrapada, Revatī.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_nakshatra_gloss: For trade (srag-vikraya / vipaṇi) the auspicious stars are Dhruva (Rohiṇī, the three Uttarās), Mṛdu (Mṛgaśira, Revatī, Chitrā, Anurādhā), Kṣipra (Hasta, Aśvinī, Puṣya) and Chara (Svātī, Punarvasu, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā) — 16 in all. The same verse also names Riktā and Bhauma (Tuesday) among the prohibitions.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_tithi: Tithi — 2,3,5,7,10,11,13 of both pakṣas; Pūrṇimā also accepted.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_tithi_gloss: Riktā (4,9,14) are inauspicious for śubha work; Pakṣa-randhra (4,6,8,9,12,14) are likewise dropped. What remains are 2,3,5,7,10,11,13 and Pūrṇimā (15) — the system's tithi list.
x.byaparik_pratisthan_vara_gloss: Per Pitāmaha (Brahmā), Tuesday is inauspicious; Saturn and Mars are krūra vāra — for a business opening Sun/Tue/Sat are dropped, keeping Mon, Wed, Thu and Fri. Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi 2.17 likewise bars Bhauma (Tuesday).
x.griha_aarambha_adhikmasa: Adhik-māsa (Malmāsa) — vāstu karma (house construction) is barred; no foundation-laying during malimluca.
x.griha_aarambha_adhikmasa_gloss: Upākarma, utsarjana, aṣṭakā-śrāddha, gṛha-praveśa, cūḍākarma, bratabandha (mauñjī-bandhana), vivāha, tīrtha-yātrā and vāstu karma — all barred in Malmāsa. When Guru/Śukra are combust, bāla or vṛddha, and malimluca runs, vāstu karma is prohibited.
x.griha_aarambha_chaturmasa: Construction is not paused during Chaturmāsa, so it is not barred here.
x.griha_aarambha_chaturmasa_gloss: Dharma Sindhu does not explicitly ban continuing construction in Chaturmāsa — that season is strict mainly for vivāha, bratabandha and pratiṣṭhā. The system does not apply a Chaturmāsa filter to vāstu construction; new gṛha-praveśa still weighs Chaturmāsa/Adhik-māsa.
x.griha_aarambha_chaturmasa_source: Dharma Sindhu 1 — Malmāse Varjyāni (Prathama Pariccheda · scope of the ban list)
x.griha_aarambha_durmuhurta: Dur-muhūrta skips only the affected period (not the whole day); Sankrānti (ordinary ±6h, cardinal ±16h) and the eclipse day are barred.
x.griha_aarambha_durmuhurta_gloss: Classically, time around Sankrānti is rejected (ghaṭī values vary by edition). The system applies this practically as ±6h ordinary and ±16h cardinal buffers; Dur-muhūrta slices and the eclipse day are also skipped.
x.griha_aarambha_graha: Graha — Jupiter & Venus must not be combust (ast), bāla or vṛddha (Dharma Sindhu applies this to vāstu karma).
x.griha_aarambha_graha_gloss: When Jupiter or Venus is combust (asta), bāla, vṛddha or during malimluca, auspicious works are barred. Seven days before setting is vṛddha; seven days after rising is bāla — the medium rule. The system applies the same combust and bāla/vṛddha filter to vāstu karma.
x.griha_aarambha_graha_source: Dharma Sindhu 1 (Prathama Pariccheda · Śukrāsta) · Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi 1.47
x.griha_aarambha_lagna: Lagna — fixed (Vṛṣa, Siṃha, Vṛśchika, Kumbha) preferred, dual accepted; movable lagnas barred — so the building is stable.
x.griha_aarambha_lagna_gloss: House construction should be done in a fixed lagna; movable lagna must never be chosen. Dual-natured lagna is acceptable if free from lagna defects. Per vāstu tradition, a fixed lagna is favoured for the building's stability. The system drops movable lagnas and keeps dual (dvisvabhāva) acceptable.
x.griha_aarambha_lagna_strength: Lagna strength & planetary yoga — Sun in 7th, Mercury in 4th, Venus in 3rd and Jupiter in lagna ensure hundred-hundred years' stability.
x.griha_aarambha_lagna_strength_gloss: When Jupiter is in lagna, Sun in the 7th, Mercury in the 4th and Venus in the 3rd, that house's lifespan is one hundred years; and another hundred years is said (i.e. hundred-hundred = two hundred). This classical yoga ensures the house's longevity and prosperity.
x.griha_aarambha_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — mṛdu/dhruva/cara/kṣipra set: Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśira, Punarvasu, U.Phalgunī, Hasta, Chitrā, Svātī, Anurādhā, U.Aṣāḍhā, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, U.Bhādrapada, Revatī.
x.griha_aarambha_nakshatra_gloss: From the verse: Mṛdu (Mṛgaśira, Revatī, Chitrā, Anurādhā), Ku/Rohiṇī, Dhruva (the three Uttarās), Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣā), Māruta (Svātī), Dhaniṣṭhā, Kara (Hasta), Tiṣya (Puṣya) — house-start in these 13 stars is 'śubhada' (giver of happiness). The verse's second half adds that foundation-digging (khāta) and the Vāstu Pūjā are likewise auspicious in these stars. Punarvasu and Śravaṇa are accepted because Nepali panchāṅga and other vāstu traditions admit them — they are not taken from this quoted verse.
x.griha_aarambha_nakshatra_source: Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi — Vāstu prakaraṇa ch. 12, verse 15 (Ācārya Śrīrāma / Rāma Daivajña)
x.griha_aarambha_solar_month: Sun-sign — Meṣa, Vṛṣabha, Siṃha, Vṛśchika, Makara or Kumbha (Vasiṣṭha’s view).
x.griha_aarambha_solar_month_gloss: Vasiṣṭha’s verse is the system’s main basis — Sun in Meṣa, Vṛṣabha, Siṃha, Vṛśchika, Makara or Kumbha makes starting a house wealth- and comfort-giving. Ch. 12 verse 16 states general Sun-fruits («caitre’rke meṣage lābho… māghe kumbhagate lābhaḥ…»); though Vṛṣabha/Vṛśchika are often dropped in that general fruit scheme, Chintāmaṇi’s own commentary cites Vasiṣṭha (and Manthara et al.) favouring these six signs — our list follows that.
x.griha_aarambha_time_window: Time — foundation-laying is a daytime rite (sunrise→sunset only).
x.griha_aarambha_time_window_gloss: Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi directs that foundation-laying be done in daytime, not at night. The system applies this as a sunrise→sunset scan.
x.griha_aarambha_tithi: Tithi — only Pratipadā (1), rikta (4,9,14) and Amāvasyā are barred; all the rest (Pūrṇimā included) are allowed. The gate is lenient — a house-start is not a marriage-grade saṃskāra.
x.griha_aarambha_tithi_gloss: The classical prohibition covers Sunday/Tuesday, rikta (4,9,14), parva (8,14,15), Amāvasyā and Pratipadā. Our lenient gate: only Pratipadā, rikta and Amāvasyā are barred — the rest qualify (inspired by the śāstra, applied this way by the system).
x.griha_aarambha_vara: Vāra — in the classical list, Tuesday and Saturday are barred; all other weekdays are acceptable.
x.griha_aarambha_vara_gloss: Per Pitāmaha (Brahmā), Tuesday is inauspicious; Saturn and Mars are krūra vāras — in gṛha-cakra (house construction) Sunday, Tuesday, parva, Amāvasyā and Pratipadā are barred. Though Sunday is also mentioned in the prohibition, in Nepali tradition and the system's practical rule, Sunday is accepted; only Tuesday and Saturday are barred.
x.griha_aarambha_yoga_gloss: This verse lists several defects to avoid in auspicious work, including Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti. On that classical basis, our system applies Vyatīpāta and Vaidhṛti as yoga defects.
x.griha_pravesh_dosha: Doṣa — Dagdha, Śūnya, malefic Latta (Sun/Mars/Saturn/Rāhu/Ketu), Dur-muhūrta (period only), Sankrānti and the eclipse day excluded.
x.griha_pravesh_dosha_source: Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi — eclipse 1.32, Dagdha 1.8, Śūnya 1.10, mahā-doṣa 1.34 (Śubhāśubha Prakaraṇa)
x.griha_pravesh_graha: Graha — Jupiter & Venus must not be combust (ast), bāla or vṛddha (Dharma Sindhu applies this to vāstu karma); Moon not in the 2/4/5/8/9/12 house from the lagna.
x.griha_pravesh_graha_gloss: When Jupiter or Venus is combust (asta), bāla, vṛddha or during malimluca, auspicious works are barred. Seven days before setting is vṛddha; seven days after rising is bāla — the medium rule. The system applies the same combust and bāla/vṛddha filter to gṛha-praveśa.
x.griha_pravesh_lagna: Lagna — only fixed (sthira) and dual (dvisvabhāva) ascendants accepted; movable ascendants rejected.
x.griha_pravesh_month: Month — only Māgha, Phālguna, Chaitra, Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha, Mārgaśīrṣa; Adhik-māsa & Chaturmāsa barred.
x.griha_pravesh_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — the conservative 8 (sthira/mṛdu): Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśira, U.Phalgunī, Chitrā, Anurādhā, U.Aṣāḍhā, U.Bhādrapada, Revatī. (If a year has fewer than 12 days, Hasta, Svātī, Śravaṇa & Dhaniṣṭhā are also admitted.)
x.griha_pravesh_surya_bala: Surya Bala — Sun not in Mithuna, Vṛśchika or Mīna (Malamas-like).
x.griha_pravesh_tithi: Tithi — only the śukla-pakṣa growth tithis 2,3,5,7,10,11,13; rikta, Amāvasyā and Pratipadā barred.
x.griha_pravesh_yoga_karana: Yoga/Karaṇa — Vyatīpāta & Vaidhṛti yoga and Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) karaṇa barred.
x.mc_1_34_gloss: Birth star/month/tithi, Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā (Viṣṭi), Vaidhṛti, Amāvasyā, parental-death days, a fortnight with two lost tithis (13-day pakṣa), Adhik-māsa and related defects are barred as mahā-doṣa for auspicious rites.
x.mc_1_3_tithisha_gloss: The presiding deities of the tithis in order — Aṣṭamī and Chaturdaśī are ruled by Śiva, so these tithis are held naturally suited to Śiva worship.
x.mc_2_36_agnivasa_gloss: Add 1 to the tithi, then the weekday; divide by 4. Remainder 3 (guṇa) or 0 places Agni on Earth (bhūvi) — the homa brings happiness. Remainder 1 (śaśi) = Heaven (loss of life); remainder 2 (gugma) = Pātāla (loss of wealth).
x.mc_2_36_agnivasa_phala_gloss: Remainder 1 (rūpe) — Agni in Heaven (vyoman), destroys wealth and life. Remainder 2 (dvik) — in Pātāla, destroys accumulated wealth. Remainder 3 or 0 (guṇa–veda) — on Earth (bhūmi), gives abundant happiness.
x.mc_2_36_nitya_gloss: Per the sages, for Nitya (regular) and Naimittika (occasional) rites — such as a general Rudrābhiṣeka — for annual observances, saṃskāras and Vaiṣṇava acts, this Agni-vāsa need not be strictly considered.
x.mc_5_16_gloss: A boy's annaprāśana falls in an even month after birth (6,8,10,12) and a girl's in an odd month (5,7,9,11); in Mṛdu, Laghu, Chara and Sthira nakṣatras; excluding Rikta (4,9,14), Nanda (1,6,11), Aṣṭamī, Amāvasyā and Dvādaśī; and avoiding Sun (Arka), Tue (Kuja) and Sat (Arki).
x.mc_5_17_gloss: Benefics in a kendra (1,4,7,10), trikoṇa (5,9) or the 11th (āya); the 10th house (kha) empty; malefics in the upachaya houses (3,6,11); and the Moon NOT in the 1st (lagna), 6th or 8th (mṛtyu) — such lagna-śuddhi is ideal.
x.mc_5_asta_gloss: Sīmanta, Jātakarma, Nāmakaraṇa, Annaprāśana and similar time-bound (nitya) saṃskāras may be performed even when Jupiter or Venus is combust (asta) — they are exceptions to the asta-doṣa.
x.mc_gp_grahana_gloss: The period around an eclipse (solar/lunar) — typically three days before and after — is barred for auspicious work.
x.mc_gp_lagna_gloss: Construction and entry should always be done in a fixed (sthira) lagna, never in a movable (chara) one; a dual (dvisvabhāva) sign is acceptable if free of other defects. (attributed to Sage Vasiṣṭha)
x.mc_gp_month_gloss: Gṛha-praveśa is auspicious in Jyeṣṭha, Māgha, Phālguna, Vaiśākha (and Mārgaśīrṣa), during Uttarāyaṇa (Saumyāyana), in a fixed (sthira) lagna, and in the Mṛdu/Dhruva/Miśra/Kṣipra/Chara nakṣatras. (For a house covered in grass/straw, entry may also be done in Dakṣiṇāyana.)
x.mc_gp_nak_gloss: Gṛha-praveśa is auspicious in the Mṛdu, Dhruva (fixed), Miśra, Kṣipra (Laghu) and Chara nakṣatra classes.
x.mc_gp_sun_gloss: The Sun-sign result: Meṣa (Chaitra) gain, Vṛṣabha (Jyeṣṭha) death, Siṃha (Bhādra) gain, Tulā (Kārtika) death, Vṛśchika (Mārgaśīrṣa) death, Makara (Pauṣa) wealth, Kumbha (Māgha) gain, Mīna (Phālguna) death. Accordingly the system bars the Sun in Mithuna, Vṛśchika or Mīna (Malamas-like / death-result).
x.mc_gp_tithi_gloss: In the gṛha-chakra, rikta (4,9,14), Amāvasyā and Pratipadā are barred. Beyond these the system keeps only the śukla-pakṣa growth tithis 2,3,5,7,10,11,13.
x.rudri_agni_vasa: Agni-vāsa — for the homa the fire must be on Earth: (tithi + vāra + 1) mod 4 ∈ {0,3} is auspicious (remainder 1 = Heaven, 2 = Pātāla — inauspicious).
x.rudri_nitya_naimittika: For Nitya/Naimittika rites (a general Rudrābhiṣeka) the Agni-vāsa check is not strictly mandatory — per the sages.
x.rudri_shiva_vasa: Śiva-vāsa — on the absolute tithi (1–30), (2×tithi+5) mod 7 ∈ {1,2,3} (Kailāsa/Gaurī/Nandi) is auspicious.
x.rudri_shiva_vasa_barred: Sabhā, Bhojana, Krīḍā, Śmaśāna (remainders 4/5/6/0) avoided; Amāvasyā excluded.
x.rudri_shiva_vasa_barred_gloss: Remainder 4 = Sabhā (progeny trouble), 5 = Bhojana (wealth loss), 6 = Krīḍā (illness), 0 or 7 = Śmaśāna (death-like inauspiciousness) — all barred. Amāvasyā is always excluded for Rudri.
x.rudri_shiva_vasa_barred_source: Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi / Dharma Sindhu (Śiva-vāsa fruits · Amāvasyā)
x.rudri_shiva_vasa_gloss: Double the current tithi and add 5; divide by 7 — the remainder is Śiva's abode. Remainder 1 = Kailāsa, 2 = with Gaurī, 3 = mounted on the bull/Nandi — all three auspicious. Computed on the sunrise tithi.
x.rudri_sunrise_panchanga: Evaluated on the day's sunrise panchāṅga — no lagna window is needed.
x.rudri_sunrise_panchanga_gloss: Śiva-vāsa is based on the day's sunrise tithi. No special lagna window (as for vivāha/bratabandha) is required — Rudri may be done throughout a day when Śiva-vāsa is favourable.
x.rudri_tithi_month_preference: Aṣṭamī/Chaturdaśī tithi and the Śrāvaṇa/Kārtika months are especially favoured (a preference, not a gate); Chandra/Tārā Bala is native-specific.
x.rudri_yoga_karana_gloss: Vyatīpāta and Vaidhṛti (Pāta) are mahā-doṣa for all auspicious rites. Never do a maṅgala act in Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) — abhiṣeka in that karaṇa destroys the work.
x.vivah_dosha: Doṣa — Dagdha, Śūnya, Bhadrā, and malefic Latta (Sun/Mars/Saturn/Rāhu/Ketu) scrub the whole day; no Godhūli rescue.
x.vivah_dosha_gloss: Defines the Latta defect, where a planet 'kicks' specific nakṣatras from its position — such days are scrubbed.
x.vivah_graha: Graha — Jupiter & Venus must be udaya — neither combust nor bāla/vṛddha (weak just after rising or before setting); Sankrānti buffers and eclipse ±3 days excluded.
x.vivah_graha_gloss: Seven days before setting is old age (vṛddha); seven days after rising is infancy (bāla) — the medium rule.
x.vivah_karana: Karaṇa — Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) and the four fixed karaṇas (Śakuni, Catuṣpāda, Nāga, Kiṃstughna) barred.
x.vivah_karana_gloss: Defines the portions of the 8th, 15th, 4th, 11th, 3rd, 10th, 7th and 14th tithis occupied by Bhadrā (Viṣṭi), which must be barred.
x.vivah_kshaya_paksha: Kṣaya Pakṣa — if a fortnight loses two tithis and becomes a 13-tithi pakṣa (atinindya), the whole period is barred; no other favourable factor overrides it.
x.vivah_kshaya_paksha_gloss: In a 13-day fortnight where two tithis are lost, 'when the pakṣa is destroyed, all is destroyed,' say all the Ācāryas.
x.vivah_month: Month — only the śāstra vivāha lunar months (Mārgaśīrṣa, Māgha, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha, Āṣāḍha); Adhik-māsa & Chaturmāsa barred.
x.vivah_month_gloss: In Mārgaśīrṣa, Māgha, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha, marriage is auspicious.
x.vivah_nakshatra: Nakṣatra — the classical 11: Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśira, Maghā, U.Phalgunī, Hasta, Svātī, Anurādhā, Mūla, U.Aṣāḍhā, U.Bhādrapada, Revatī.
x.vivah_nakshatra_gloss: Mṛgaśira, Hasta, Mūla, Anurādhā, Maghā, Rohiṇī, Revatī, the three Uttarās and Svātī are the marriage stars.
x.vivah_simhastha: Simhastha Guru — marriage is barred for the whole transit of Jupiter through Siṃha (Leo).
x.vivah_simhastha_gloss: When Jupiter is in Maghā nakṣatra or the sign Siṃha, all auspicious rites are prohibited in every region.
x.vivah_solar_month: Solar month — the Sun must be in Meṣa, Vṛṣabha, Mithuna, Vṛśchika, Makara or Kumbha (the śāstra checks the Sun-sign first).
x.vivah_solar_month_gloss: Marriage is auspicious when the Sun stands in Meṣa, Vṛṣabha, Mithuna, Vṛśchika, Makara or Kumbha.
x.vivah_tithi: Tithi — only śubha tithis (2,3,5,7,10,11,13); rikta (4,9,14), Aṣṭamī, Ṣaṣṭhī, Amāvasyā, Pūrṇimā out.
x.vivah_tithi_gloss: The 4th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 12th and 14th are the Pakṣa-randhra tithis (and are barred).
x.vivah_vara_gloss: Per the Bṛhat Saṃhitā (1.4), Brahmā himself declared Tuesday inauspicious; Saturday and Tuesday are 'krūra vāra' — the Muhūrta Chintāmaṇi admits only Mon, Wed, Thu and Fri for marriage (Ravi-Kuja-Śani especially avoided).
x.vivah_yoga: Yoga — all nine aśubha yogas (Viṣkambha, Atigaṇḍa, Śūla, Gaṇḍa, Vyāghāta, Vajra, Vyatīpāta, Parigha, Vaidhṛti) barred.

wheel.heading: Direction wheel
wheel.blurb: Eight directions around a central Brahmasthan — each with its own element, presiding deity and best use. Pick a direction.

compass.dialog_body: The phone compass will turn the wheel to match the house. Stand at the exact centre of the house — the Brahmasthan — hold the phone upright in front of you, then tap Done. The wall you face will sit at the top of the ring.
compass.live: Compass live — the wall you face is at the top of the ring.
compass.drifting: This device has no absolute compass — the heading may drift.
compass.denied: Compass permission was denied. On iPhone, enable Motion & Orientation for this site in Settings.
compass.unavailable: No compass reading. Try again on a phone, over https, standing at the centre of the house.

plan.heading: House layout (2D)
plan.blurb: The Vastu Purusha Mandala — the house split into nine zones with north at the top: the Brahmasthan at the centre, the eight directions around it. Tap any zone or room.
plan.requirements_blurb: First say how many bedrooms, toilets and other spaces you need. Then the planner suggests a zone for each — preferred, acceptable, or shared — not a single locked direction.
plan.wet_blurb: A toilet, a bathroom, and a combined toilet-bath are treated as different placements in Vastu, so they are asked separately.
plan.combine_kitchen_dining_note: Classical Vastu keeps them separate because of wood-fire smoke and ash. Modern gas or electric cooking removes that concern, so combining is offered as a valid modern choice — not the default.

mode.strict_hint: Rooms stay in their recommended zones only. If those fill up, they share a zone rather than moving elsewhere.
mode.flexible_hint: When a recommended zone is full, the room may move to an acceptable alternative — never into an avoid zone.

plan.floor_blurb: If a room must stay on a particular floor, say so here. The sketch is still a single-storey plan.
plan.zoning_blurb: For each space: the recommended zone, acceptable alternatives, areas to avoid, and where this plan placed it.
plan.why_note: This is a simplified traditional guide — not a final architectural or construction plan.
plan.layout_blurb: A rough sketch of the classical courtyard house: the Brahmasthan open in the middle, the alindra gallery around it, and each room in its own compass zone.

valid.missing_door: A room is missing a door.
valid.isolated: A room is not reachable from the hall.
valid.private_through: A private room is only reached through another private room.
valid.stair: The stair does not connect every floor.
valid.kitchen_dining: Kitchen and dining are not adjacent — the plan still works, but service flow is weaker.
valid.wet_access: A wet room does not open directly onto the hall.
valid.vastu_relaxed: A strict Vastu preference conflicted with circulation or room size, so the architectural arrangement was kept.
valid.wet_separate: In strict Vastu, bathing and the latrine are not combined in one room.
valid.brahma_path: A passage must not cross the Brahmasthan; it should wrap around.
valid.toilet_zone: A toilet must not sit in the north-east, south-west, or Brahmasthan.

plan.cannot_fit_blurb: These rooms need more space at a usable size. Add a storey, remove rooms, or enlarge the plot.

why.master_bedroom: Southwest is treated as a stable earth zone — traditionally the householder's rest and authority sit here.
why.bedroom: West, northwest or south are usual for other bedrooms; northeast and southeast are traditionally kept lighter.
why.toilet: Waste is kept toward the airy west/northwest and away from the northeast and the central Brahmasthan.
why.bathroom: Bathing is a water activity — northwest or west is usual; the sacred northeast is avoided.
why.combined: Even as one room, a toilet-bath is kept off the northeast and center, toward the air zone.
why.living: A living room wants morning light and a welcoming path — north or east first.
why.kitchen: The kitchen is fire — the southeast Agni corner is preferred; fire is kept out of the northeast.
why.dining: Dining sits near the kitchen on the west or east; the northeast is kept open.
why.puja: Puja belongs in Ishan (northeast) — the water/space corner, facing the sunrise.
why.study: Study wants calm light — west, north or northeast; southwest is treated as too heavy.
why.office: Work and income are linked with north/northwest; southeast fire is thought to add restlessness.
why.store: Storage is heavy — southwest or south holds weight; northeast is kept light.
why.laundry: Laundry is water and air — northwest is usual; dirty water is kept off the northeast.
why.staircase: Stairs turn clockwise toward south or west; the northeast and center stay free of heavy structure.
why.garage: Vehicles sit in the airy northwest or near the fire corner; the northeast stays open.
why.guest: Guests are temporary — northwest; they are not placed in the householder's southwest.
why.family: A family room rests in the north or west; southeast fire is busier.
why.balcony: A balcony wants light and air — north, east or northeast; southwest stays more closed.
why.courtyard: A courtyard keeps the Brahmasthan or northeast open — the house's breath.
why.garden: A garden is green water-light in the northeast, north or east; large trees are kept off the southwest.
why.servant: A service room sits northwest or west — apart from the northeast and the householder's corner.
why.gym: Exercise belongs in the active west or south; the northeast stays quiet.
why.library: A library likes quiet light in the north, northeast or west; southeast is busier.

rooms.heading: Room by direction
rooms.blurb: The question asked most while building or arranging a home — where each room belongs.

checker.no_selection: Select each room's actual direction below to see your score.

element_tip.earth: Keep this area heavier and well-ordered — earthy tones or solid furniture help balance it.
element_tip.water: Light blue or black accents, or a small water feature, help balance this direction.
element_tip.fire: Good lighting or warm red/orange accents bring out this direction's element.
element_tip.air: Keep this space open and light — avoid storing heavy items here.
element_tip.space: Keep this space as open and clutter-free as possible.

plot.heading: Plan your plot
plot.blurb: Enter the plot’s length and breadth, then which way the main door faces. The house plan is drawn on that rectangle.
plot.range_error: Enter a value between {{min}} and {{max}} meters.
plot.invalid_shape: These four lengths can't close into a plot — the east/west walls are too short to span the difference between north and south. Try adjusting the values.
plot.buffer_note: The house plan uses the length × breadth rectangle you entered. Leave setback or garden as a separate strip if you need it.
plot.ayadi_disclaimer: A simplified version of one traditional method — not a substitute for a qualified Vastu consultant.
plot.ayadi_suggestion: Try a width of {{hasta}} hasta (~{{meters}} m) instead for an auspicious remainder.
plot.entrance_disclaimer: A general rule of thumb — the exact corner and the exact center are avoided regardless of facing.
plot.marma_note: The dashed lines are the plot's two main marma (energy) lines, corner to corner — traditional guidance keeps heavy pillars, walls, or toilets off them. This shows just the two main diagonals, not the complete traditional marma/rajju system.

sketch.door_pada: Main door — pada {{n}} ({{pada}}) of the {{wall}} wall
sketch.rule_court: Brahmasthana: the centre stays open to the sky as a courtyard — nothing is built in it [Samarangana Sutradhara 13:22].
sketch.rule_alindra: Alindra: a covered gallery rings the court on all four sides, so every room is reached without crossing it [Mayamata 26:15].

dosha.heading: Vastu dosha & remedies
dosha.blurb: A finished house rarely needs rebuilding — most doshas have a simple correction.

northeast_fire.problem: Kitchen or toilet in the north-east
northeast_fire.remedy: Move the kitchen to the south-east if you can. If not, keep that corner spotless, place water in a copper vessel there and use light colours.

center_heavy.problem: Staircase, toilet or heavy structure in the Brahmasthan
center_heavy.remedy: Keep the centre clear. Where it cannot be removed, add light, keep only light furniture and let the floor read as open.

southwest_light.problem: A south-west corner left open, light or full of windows
southwest_light.remedy: Add weight there — a heavy wardrobe or store; make the windows smaller or hang heavy curtains.

northeast_heavy.problem: Heavy load or clutter in the north-east
northeast_heavy.remedy: Keep the north-east light and open — clear shoes, waste and heavy items; a small water feature or green plant suits it.

head_north.problem: Sleeping with your head to the north
head_north.remedy: Turn the bed so your head points south or east — sleep is said to settle deeper.

blocked_door.problem: A pillar, tree or clutter blocking the main door
blocked_door.remedy: Keep the entry open, lit and clean; repair a door that creaks or sticks.

nne.name: North-Northeast
nne.importance: NNE — water and sattva. The zone that strengthens the body and the effect of medicine; the classical oshadhagriha.
nne.best: First-aid, medicine storage, a light exercise room
nne.avoid: Toilet, a waste dump, a heavy overhead tank

ene.name: East-Northeast
ene.importance: ENE — air and sattva. Joy, freshness and social energy. This is the east wind, not Īśāna.
ene.best: Garden, large windows, a light sitting area, play

ese.name: East-Southeast
ese.importance: ESE — air and rajas. This slice is mental churning; sitting here feeds overthinking.
ese.best: Washing machine, a churning/work nook, an informal talk room
ese.avoid: Meditation room, puja, a sleeping bed

sse.name: South-Southeast
sse.importance: SSE — fire and tamas. It drives off fear and gives bodily strength and confidence.
sse.best: Gym, a guard room, sports storage

ssw.name: South-Southwest
ssw.importance: SSW — earth and tamas. The main disposal slice; its energy helps the house shed waste and the negative.
ssw.best: Toilet, septic, dustbin, a waste dump
ssw.avoid: Puja, a safe, kitchen, the main bed

wsw.name: West-Southwest
wsw.importance: WSW — space and tamas. The principal slice for study and for keeping savings.
wsw.avoid: Toilet, a gas stove, disposal fittings

wnw.name: West-Northwest
wnw.importance: WNW — space and rajas. The slice that throws grief and the negative out; classically a rodanagriha, a weeping-room.
wnw.best: Washing machine, toilet, waste store, a quiet sit for the mind
wnw.avoid: Puja, a new bride's room, a deep-rest bedroom

nnw.name: North-Northwest
nnw.importance: NNW — air and sattva. The couple's attraction and affection; classically a ratigriha.
nnw.best: A newlyweds' bedroom, dressing room, a place for scents

n.name: North
n.importance: N — water and sattva. Kubera's quarter. It draws new work and a steady inflow of money.
n.best: Main door, office, a money safe, an open living room

ne.name: Ishana
ne.quality: Clarity of mind and the spiritual
ne.importance: NE — water and sattva. The head of the house, where cosmic energy enters; it gives mental clarity and spiritual lift.
ne.best: Puja room, meditation, yoga, an open courtyard
ne.avoid: Toilet, heavy storage, kitchen, an overhead water tank

e.name: East
e.importance: E — air and sattva. It governs reach and ties in society. Morning sun from here puts prana into the house.
e.best: Bathroom, an east-facing main door, living room
e.avoid: Heavy cupboards, toilet, a closed southwest-like wall

se.name: Agneya
se.importance: SE — fire and rajas. It governs cash liquidity and the household's digestive fire.
se.best: Main kitchen, electrical meter, generator, heater

s.name: South
s.importance: S — earth and tamas. The slice of rest and deep sleep; it eases the day's fatigue and quiets the mind.
s.best: Bedroom, heavy cupboards, a higher south wall
s.avoid: A well or boring, puja, an open courtyard

sw.name: Nairitya
sw.importance: SW — earth and tamas. It steadies family bonds and a person's working skill.
sw.best: Master bedroom, heavy cupboards, a jewellery locker
sw.avoid: Toilet, underground water, main door, an open balcony

w.name: West
w.importance: W — space and tamas. Trade profit, the fruit of work, and the nourishment of a meal.
w.best: Dining room, a west-facing main door, a safe
w.avoid: Toilet, a disposal zone, junk storage

nw.name: Vayavya
nw.importance: NW — air and rajas. Help from neighbours, banks and society; the carrier of wind.
nw.best: Guest room, grain store, vehicle parking
nw.avoid: A heavy RCC pillar, master bedroom, a badly placed septic

soma.name: Soma
soma.deity: Soma (the moon — coolness and mental peace)
soma.best: Main door, meditation, a light sitting room, a place for gems

bhujaga.name: Bhujanga
bhujaga.deity: Bhujanga (a guardian naga / northern water deity)
bhujaga.best: First-aid, medicine storage, a light exercise room
bhujaga.avoid: Toilet, a heavy overhead tank, junk

aditi.name: Aditi
aditi.deity: Aditi (mother of the gods — protection and the boundless)
aditi.best: A light sitting room, meditation, puja, a north door

diti.name: Diti
diti.deity: Diti (mother of the asuras — foresight and resolve)
diti.best: Study, a child's bed, a light window

shikhi.name: Shikhi
shikhi.best: Meditation, puja, a lightly ventilated window, open space
shikhi.avoid: Main door (fear of fire and grief), toilet, kitchen, heavy storage

parjanya.name: Parjanya
parjanya.best: Underground water tank, garden, a large window, a light sitting room
parjanya.avoid: Toilet, junk storage, a heavy RCC pillar

jayanta.name: Jayanta
jayanta.best: Main door (highly auspicious — wealth and children), study, living room
jayanta.avoid: Toilet, a waste dump, a heavy overhead tank

mahendra.name: Mahendra
mahendra.best: Main entrance (honour and fame), living room, office

surya.name: Surya
surya.best: Bathroom with morning sun, a large window, a yoga room
surya.avoid: Main door (anger and pride), a sleeping bed, heavy furniture

satya.name: Satya
satya.best: Living room, a place for social visits, windows
satya.avoid: Main door (fear of deceit from outsiders), filth

bhrisha.name: Bhrisha
bhrisha.deity: Bhrisha (feeling, desire and the sun's heat)
bhrisha.best: Washing machine, cupboards, a laundry spot
bhrisha.avoid: Master bedroom, puja, main door (excess anger and cruelty)

aakasha.name: Antariksha
aakasha.avoid: Main door (theft and sudden loss), underground water

anila.name: Anila

anila.avoid: Main door (harm to children and fire), underground water

pushan.name: Pushan

pushan.avoid: Main door (servitude and hard labour), puja

vitatha.name: Vitatha

vitatha.avoid: Main door (moral decline and lying), puja

grihakshata.name: Grihakshata

grihakshata.avoid: Underground water, septic, an open gap

yama.name: Yama
yama.best: A heavy RCC pillar, iron storage, stairs
yama.avoid: Main door (chronic illness and untimely death), puja

gandharva.name: Gandharva
gandharva.best: A music or leisure room, living room, guest bedroom
gandharva.avoid: The main safe (money is hard to keep), a junk room

bhringraj.name: Bhringraj
bhringraj.avoid: Master bedroom (bodily weakness), puja, main door

mriga.name: Mriga

mriga.avoid: Main door (loss of children and wealth), an open balcony

pitra.name: Pitra

pitra.avoid: Main door (loss of lifespan and wealth), toilet, a water boring

dauvarika.name: Dauvarika
dauvarika.best: A guard room, study, a rear service gate
dauvarika.avoid: The main safe, an open balcony

sugriva.name: Sugriva
sugriva.best: A children's study, bookcase, grain store

pushpadanta.name: Pushpadanta
pushpadanta.best: A west-facing main door (highly auspicious — lineage and wealth), dining room

varuna.name: Varuna
varuna.best: Dining room, overhead water tank, a west door
varuna.avoid: A toilet septic, a junk pile

asura.name: Asura
asura.best: Toilet, septic, a junk room, dustbin
asura.avoid: Puja, master bedroom, main door (quarrel and insult)

shosha.name: Shosha
shosha.deity: Shosha (the power that dries or drains energy)
shosha.best: Toilet, an oven, or dry-goods storage

papayakshma.name: Papayakshma
papayakshma.avoid: Main door (illness and hardship), kitchen, puja

roga.name: Roga
roga.best: A waste spot, septic, an outlet pipe
roga.avoid: Bedroom (chronic illness), main door, a well

naga.name: Naga
naga.avoid: Main door (an enemy's plot), puja, bedroom

mukhya.name: Mukhya
mukhya.best: A north-facing main door (highly auspicious — wealth and ease), study
mukhya.avoid: Toilet, heavy cupboards, kitchen (fire against water)

bhallata.name: Bhallata
bhallata.best: Main entrance (great wealth and land), a locker, a safe
bhallata.avoid: Toilet, kitchen, a heavy RCC pillar

bhudhara.name: Bhudhara
bhudhara.importance: Bhudhara — the inner deity of the north. The earth-bearer; stability at the core, not a wall pada.
bhudhara.best: An open core toward the living room

aryama.name: Aryama
aryama.importance: Aryama — the inner deity of the east. Solar honour; the core of social life and the door.
aryama.best: Light, air, the core toward the entrance

vivasvan.name: Vivasvan
vivasvan.importance: Vivasvan — the inner deity of the south. The dharma-sun; the core of a heavy base.
vivasvan.best: A firm floor, the core toward heavy rooms

mitra.name: Mitra
mitra.importance: Mitra — the inner deity of the west. The core of contracts and gain.
mitra.best: The core toward a study, an open west

east.name: East
east.importance: Indra and Aryama in the east — air and sattva. Morning prana, social life and vitality enter here; do not block the sun or the breeze.
east.best: Main door, large windows, wherever morning light should reach
east.avoid: Blocking it with tall walls or heavy structures

southeast.name: South-East
southeast.importance: Agneya — the seat of rajas and fire. Cooking, digestion and electrical heat belong here; do not let water oppose it.

south.name: South
south.importance: Yama and Vivasvan — the southern seat of fire and tamas. Strength, security and bedrooms; not the main door or a wide gap.
south.avoid: A large open gap, or the main entrance

southwest.name: South-West
southwest.importance: Nairitya — earth and tamas, the Vastu Purusha's feet. The house's heavy stability, the master bedroom and the ground of the household.
southwest.best: Master bedroom, the heaviest part of the house, overhead water tank
southwest.avoid: Open courtyard, large windows, underground water

west.name: West
west.importance: West — space, Varuna and Mitra. Gains, dining and contemplation; not as hollow as the Brahmasthan, and not the main shrine.

northwest.name: North-West
northwest.importance: Vayavya — air and rajas, motion and change. Guests, toilet and vehicles belong here; a permanent master bedroom stays restless.
northwest.avoid: Master bedroom — it is held to keep the mind restless

north.name: North
north.importance: Kubera's quarter — wealth, opportunity and cool water energy. A living room or treasury here keeps income flowing; do not weigh it down.
north.best: Treasury or safe, living room, water source, open and light space

northeast.name: North-East
northeast.importance: The Vastu Purusha's head — the root of water and sattva. Health, clarity and Isha live here; keep this the lightest, most sacred corner.
northeast.best: Puja room, underground water tank, well — the most sacred corner of a home

center.name: Brahmasthan
center.importance: Brahmasthan — space and sattva. Every direction unfolds from here; a pillar, stair or heavy load blocks Brahma's breath.
center.best: Open, lit and empty — the part of the house that breathes

main_door.name: Main door
main_door.note: East or north is best; the door should open inward and the approach stay clear.

kitchen.name: Kitchen
kitchen.note: Face east while cooking; keep stove and sink apart — fire and water clash.

master_bedroom.name: Master bedroom
master_bedroom.note: Sleep with your head to the south or east; no mirror facing the bed.

puja.name: Puja room
puja.note: Face the murti east or west; never share a wall with a toilet.

living.name: Living room
living.note: Keep the north-east open and light; heavy furniture to the south-west.

study.name: Study
study.note: Face east or north while studying; a wall behind the desk, not a window.

bathroom.name: Toilet & bath
bathroom.note: Never in the north-east or the centre; keep the door closed.

staircase.name: Staircase
staircase.note: Rising clockwise; never through the middle of the house.

water_tank.name: Water tank
water_tank.note: Underground tank in the north-east, overhead tank in the south-west or west.

storage.name: Storage

intro: This Nepali date converter switches instantly between Bikram Sambat (BS) and Gregorian (AD) dates. It is the fastest way to verify a birth date, fill in citizenship, passport or academic documents, and align the Nepali and English calendars.

Bikram Sambat is Nepal's official calendar, running about 56 years and 8 months ahead of the Gregorian calendar. Because the length of each Nepali month changes from year to year, accurate conversion needs the official calendar tables — which is exactly what this tool uses.

items.q: How many years apart are BS and AD dates?
items.a: Bikram Sambat runs about 56 years 8 months ahead of the Gregorian calendar. For example, AD {{adYear}} corresponds to BS {{bsYear}}. The Nepali new year starts on Baisakh 1 (mid-April).

items.q: How do I convert a Nepali date to English?
items.a: Choose BS → AD mode above and pick the year, month and day — the English date, weekday and full details appear instantly. AD → BS works the same way in reverse.
Conversions are based on the official Nepali calendar month tables, so results are reliable for birth dates, documents and official use.

items.q: How many days are in a Nepali month?
items.a: Nepali months have 29 to 32 days, and the count can differ each year because months are set by the sun's zodiac transition (sankranti).
All commonly used BS/AD years are supported — from historical dates to upcoming years.

intro: The almanac is the heart of the Vedic calendar — its five limbs (tithi, vara, nakshatra, yoga and karana) describe the religious and astrological character of each day. This page shows today's tithi, moon sign, sunrise–sunset, moonrise and auspicious times in full detail.
Calculations are based on astronomical ephemeris positions, so tithi start and end times are accurate to the minute. Use the daily almanac to plan fasts, pujas, shraddha and auspicious ceremonies.

items.q: How do I find today's tithi?
items.a: Today's tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana are shown automatically on this page. A tithi is defined by the sun–moon angular distance, so it can change mid-day; the exact start and end times are listed too.

items.q: What are the five limbs of the almanac?
items.a: Tithi, vara (weekday), nakshatra, yoga and karana — together these five make up the almanac, and festivals and auspicious times are set from them.

items.q: What are tithi vriddhi and tithi kshaya?
items.a: When the same tithi spans two sunrises it is vriddhi (repeated); when a tithi touches no sunrise it is kshaya (skipped). This is why the Nepali calendar sometimes repeats or skips a tithi.

items.q: Which location is this almanac calculated for?
items.a: By default it follows Kathmandu sunrise; if you allow location access, timings adjust to your own city's sunrise and sunset.
A moment is a window when the almanac limbs align favourably — weddings, bratabandha and house-warming are traditionally timed to it. Abhijit moment and daily sait are available in this patro.

tithi.what: A tithi is a lunar day — one of the 30 phases of the Moon in a lunar month. It is the time the Moon takes to gain 12° of angular separation (elongation) from the Sun.
tithi.how: Computed from the difference between the Moon's and Sun's ecliptic longitudes. Each 12° of that gap is one tithi (30 tithis × 12° = 360°). Because it depends on the Moon's varying speed, a tithi can be shorter or longer than a solar day; the exact begin/end instants are found where the elongation crosses each multiple of 12°.
tithi.meaning: The tithi governs most festivals, fasts (Ekadashi, Purnima, Aaushi) and muhurta selection. Shukla paksha (waxing) tithis 1–15 lead to the full moon; Krishna paksha (waning) tithis 1–15 lead to the new moon.

nakshatra.what: A nakshatra is one of the 27 lunar mansions — equal 13°20′ divisions of the zodiac through which the Moon passes, occupying each for roughly a day.
nakshatra.how: The ecliptic (360°) is divided into 27 equal arcs of 13°20′. After applying the Lahiri ayanamsha, the nakshatra is read from the Moon's sidereal longitude; begin/end times are the instants the Moon crosses each 13°20′ boundary.
nakshatra.meaning: The nakshatra drives the birth star (janma nakshatra), tarabala, and muhurta. Each is ruled by a deity and a planet and carries its own nature (fixed, movable, fierce, and so on).

yoga.what: A (nitya) yoga is one of 27 Sun–Moon combinations. It is not a physical position but a value derived from their combined longitudes.
yoga.how: Add the Sun's and Moon's sidereal longitudes and divide the total (0–360°) into 27 equal parts of 13°20′. Each part is one yoga; begin/end are when the combined longitude crosses each boundary.
yoga.meaning: Some yogas are auspicious (Siddhi, Amrita) and some malefic (Vyatipata, Vaidhriti, the opening of Vishkumbha). Yoga is one of the five limbs of the almanac checked when choosing a muhurta.

karana.what: A karana is half of a tithi. There are 60 karanas in a lunar month, of 11 distinct types (7 movable that repeat, and 4 fixed).
karana.how: Each tithi (12° of elongation) is split into two 6° halves, and each half is a karana. The 7 movable karanas cycle round, while the 4 fixed karanas are anchored around the new moon (Aaushi).
karana.meaning: Karana refines timing within a tithi. The Vishti (Bhadra) karana is inauspicious for auspicious work; the fixed karanas (Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga, Kimstughna) are considered heavy.

chandra-rashi.what: The Moon sign is the zodiac sign (rashi) the Moon occupies — one of 12 equal 30° signs. It changes about every 2¼ days.
chandra-rashi.how: From the Moon's sidereal longitude, the rashi is longitude ÷ 30°. Transition times are the moments the Moon crosses each 30° sign boundary.
chandra-rashi.meaning: The Moon sign is the basis of Vedic rashiphal (horoscope), chandrabala, and the janma rashi used in naming and matchmaking.

choghadiya.what: Choghadiya divides the day (sunrise→sunset) and night (sunset→sunrise) into 8 muhurtas each — 16 slots ruled in turn by planets, each marked good, bad, or neutral.
choghadiya.how: Daylight is split into 8 equal parts and night into 8 equal parts, so each part's length varies with the season. The ruling planet of each slot follows a fixed sequence starting from the weekday's lord, and the planet's nature sets the quality.
choghadiya.meaning: A quick, popular muhurta guide for daily tasks and travel — pick a Shubha/Amrita/Labha slot and avoid Roga/Kala/Udvega.

hora.what: Hora is the planetary hour — the 24 hours of a day, each ruled by one of the 7 planets (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn).
hora.how: Day and night are divided into planetary hours from sunrise. The first hora of the day is ruled by the weekday's lord, then the sequence follows the Chaldean order, each hora advancing by one planet.
hora.meaning: Choose a hora whose ruling planet suits the task (Jupiter for study, Venus for the arts, Mercury for trade), and avoid malefic horas (Saturn, Mars, Sun) for delicate work.

lagna.what: Lagna (the ascendant) is the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a given moment. Over a day all 12 signs rise in turn.
lagna.how: Computed from the local sidereal time and the observer's latitude — the point of the ecliptic crossing the eastern horizon. Each sign's rising duration differs by latitude and by sign (short and long ascension).
lagna.meaning: The lagna is the first house of a chart and the anchor for muhurta and kundali; the sign rising at an event's time shapes its outcome.

udaya-lagna.what: Udaya Lagna lists the exact clock times each ascendant sign rises through the day, and flags the Pushkara Navamsha moments within them.
udaya-lagna.how: The same ascendant maths as Lagna, but presented as a table of rising→setting times for each sign, with the Pushkara navamsha degrees (auspicious sub-divisions) marked where they fall.
udaya-lagna.meaning: Used to pin a muhurta to the exact rising-sign window, and to catch the auspicious Pushkara moments for important beginnings.

chandrabala.what: Chandrabala ("Moon strength") measures how favourable the Moon's current sign is relative to a person's birth Moon sign.
chandrabala.how: Count signs from the birth Moon sign (janma rashi) to the Moon's transit sign. Positions 2, 5, 7, 9, 11 (and others by tradition) are strong and favourable; 1, 3, 6, 10 are weaker — tabulated for each rashi.
chandrabala.meaning: A strong Chandrabala day supports travel, ceremonies and new work; weak Chandrabala warns that rashi to be cautious.

tarabala.what: Tarabala ("star strength") rates the day's nakshatra against a person's birth nakshatra through the nine-tara cycle.
tarabala.how: Count from the birth star to the day's star and take it modulo 9 → one of nine taras (Janma, Sampat, Vipat, Kshema, Pratyari, Sadhaka, Vadha, Mitra, Ati-mitra). Some are auspicious, some to be avoided.
tarabala.meaning: The good taras (Sampat, Kshema, Sadhaka, Mitra, Ati-mitra) favour action; Vipat, Pratyari and Vadha are avoided for important work.

panchaka-rahita.what: Panchaka Rahita shows the windows of the day free of the five "panchaka" faults (Mrityu, Agni, Raja, Chora, Roga) that make certain acts inauspicious.
panchaka-rahita.how: The weekday, tithi, nakshatra and lagna are combined; when their combination lands on one of the five panchaka faults it is flagged. The remaining clear time is "panchaka-rahita" (panchaka-free).
panchaka-rahita.meaning: Choose panchaka-free windows for acts the five faults specifically prohibit — roofing, travelling south, buying fuel or wood, or funerary rites.

pushkara.what: Pushkara Navamsha are especially auspicious sub-segments: specific navamsha (1/9th) divisions within certain nakshatras where the ascendant becomes "Pushkara" (nourishing).
pushkara.how: Each sign's 30° is split into nine 3°20′ navamshas; in defined sign/navamsha pairs the rising point qualifies as Pushkara. The page marks the clock moments the lagna passes through these.
pushkara.meaning: Acts begun in a Pushkara Navamsha moment (purchases, investments, foundations) are held to prosper and multiply.

graha-sthiti.what: Graha sthiti is the precise celestial position of the nine grahas (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Rahu, Ketu) and the ascendant (लग्न) at a given moment. Each planet's sign, nakshatra, pada, nakshatra lord/sub-lord, full degree, latitude (shara), speed, right ascension and declination are shown.
graha-sthiti.how: Values are computed at local sunrise from the Swiss Ephemeris. Rekhamsha and full degree are sidereal longitudes with the Lahiri ayanamsha applied; nakshatra, pada and lord/sub-lord are derived from that same sidereal longitude. Shara (latitude), right ascension and declination come from an ecliptic-to-equatorial transform and are ayanamsha-independent. Retrograde (negative speed) and combustion near the Sun are also flagged.
graha-sthiti.meaning: Graha sthiti underpins the birth chart, transits (gochar), muhurta and daily prediction. The nakshatra lord and sub-lord are used in KP (Krishnamurti Paddhati) to judge results, while declination shows a planet's north/south tilt from the celestial equator.

graha-asta.what: Graha asta is when a planet is lost in the Sun's glare and invisible in the sky. A planet becomes asta (combust) when it comes within a set angle of the Sun and rises again (udaya) when it moves away. This page lists the yearly asta windows for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, plus the Moon's monthly 'Chandra Tara Asta' (combustion near the new moon).
graha-asta.how: For planets, the sidereal elongation from the Sun is computed; when it drops below the Surya-Siddhanta graha-specific threshold (Jupiter ~11°, Venus ~10°) the planet is asta, and udaya when it rises above. Chandra Tara Asta recurs at every new moon — the Moon counts as combust on the days it lies within 13° of the Sun, with the window running from that first day's moonrise to the last day's moonset.
graha-asta.meaning: A combust planet is considered weak, so auspicious rites such as marriage and bratabandha are barred when Jupiter or Venus is asta (Guru/Shukra Tara Asta). Chandra Tara Asta is likewise avoided for some auspicious work. Once a body rises again it is regarded as strong and auspicious.

graha-vakri.what: Graha vakri (retrograde) is when a planet appears to move backward through the zodiac as seen from Earth. It is an apparent motion caused by the relative speeds of Earth and the planet. When the planet resumes forward motion it is margi (direct). This page lists the vakri/margi station moments through the year for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
graha-vakri.how: The sign of each planet's daily speed (°/day) is tracked. When the speed turns from positive to negative the planet begins retrograde (vakri station); from negative to positive it turns direct (margi). The exact instant of the sign change is found by bisection.
graha-vakri.meaning: A retrograde planet's effects are traditionally seen as intensified or altered, and matter in transit analysis. Mercury retrograde is associated with communication and travel, and Saturn retrograde with long-term karma.

surya-grahan.what: A solar eclipse is when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, and the Moon's shadow fully or partially covers the Sun. It always occurs on a new moon (Aaushi). This page lists the year's solar eclipses — their type and whether they are visible from Nepal.
surya-grahan.how: The Swiss Ephemeris eclipse-search routines compute each solar eclipse's maximum instant, type (total, annular, hybrid or partial) and local visibility for the given location within the year. For visible eclipses the local first contact (begin) and last contact (end) times are shown.
surya-grahan.meaning: In dharmashastra the eclipse period is considered inauspicious; the sutaka (fore-period) of a solar eclipse usually begins about 12 hours earlier. During it, auspicious acts, eating and touching idols are avoided, while chanting, charity and bathing are held to be meritorious.

chandra-grahan.what: A lunar eclipse is when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, and the Earth's shadow covers the Moon fully, partially or as a penumbral shading. It always occurs on a full moon (Purnima). This page lists the year's lunar eclipses — their type and whether they are visible from Nepal.
chandra-grahan.how: The Swiss Ephemeris eclipse-search routines compute each lunar eclipse's maximum instant, type (total, partial or penumbral) and whether the Moon is above the horizon (visible) from the given location within the year. For visible eclipses the partial-phase begin and end times are shown.
chandra-grahan.meaning: A lunar eclipse's sutaka period usually begins about 9 hours before the eclipse. As with a solar eclipse, auspicious acts are avoided and chanting, charity and bathing are performed. During a total lunar eclipse the Moon appears red (the ‘blood moon’).

diagrams.belt_total_width: the zodiac belt — about 18° wide in all
diagrams.belt_width_caption: The Sun is on the ecliptic by definition — its latitude is always 0°. Everything else strays: the Moon by ±5.1°, Mercury by as much as ±7°. Containing all of them takes a band about 9° either side of the ecliptic, and that band is the zodiac belt. Which is why the zodiac is a belt rather than a line.
diagrams.belt_width_label: The width of the zodiac belt — about 9° either side of the ecliptic
diagrams.day_length_caption: The H that the sunrise equation gives you is half a day. Local noon sits in the middle, sunrise at noon − H and sunset at noon + H — so one solve gives both, and day length is simply 2H. At Kathmandu H runs about 6h 55m at the summer solstice and 5h 13m at the winter one.
diagrams.day_length_label: Day length = 2H — the hour angle on either side of local noon
diagrams.eclipse_season_caption: An eclipse needs the Sun near a node of the Moon's orbit, and the Sun stays that close for about 34 days — that window is the eclipse season. Since a new Moon and a full Moon are always about 14 days apart, a 34-day window almost always catches both: a solar eclipse at new Moon and a lunar one at full. That is why eclipses arrive in pairs rather than singly.
diagrams.eclipse_season_label: The ~34-day eclipse window and the new–full Moon pair it catches
diagrams.ecliptic_cross_caption: Two great circles on one sphere must cross twice, and these cross at exactly 23.44° — the axial tilt. Those crossings are the equinoxes, and the points farthest from the equator are the solstices. So the four seasonal markers are not four separate facts: they are where two circles meet and where they are farthest apart.
diagrams.ecliptic_cross_label: The ecliptic and the celestial equator — crossing twice, parting by 23.44°
diagrams.graha_meaning_sun: Soul, father, authority — measures rashi and sankranti
diagrams.gregorian_jump_caption: Ten days were struck from October 1582 to clear the accumulated Julian error: the 4th was followed directly by the 15th, and the days between never existed anywhere. Adoption was not simultaneous, though, and because the error kept accruing, later adopters had to remove more days — eleven for Britain, thirteen for Russia.
diagrams.gregorian_jump_label: The ten days removed from October 1582, and the staggered adoption that followed
diagrams.gregorian_jump_lost_days: ten days removed — these never happened
diagrams.hierarchy_caption: Three motions, three streams, one date. Earth's spin gives the day and the vaara, the Sun's travel through the zodiac gives sankranti and the solar month, the Moon's angle from the Sun gives tithi, paksha and the lunar month — the middle two streams are exactly sauramāna and chāndramāna, and all three together make the panchanga.
diagrams.hierarchy_stacked_aria: The chain from celestial motion to the panchanga and a Bikram Sambat date.
diagrams.hierarchy_wide_aria: Earth's, the Sun's and the Moon's motions produce the day, the solar month and the lunar month; together they make the panchanga and a Bikram Sambat date.
diagrams.hora_cycle_caption: The seven grahas sit in a ring ordered by classical orbital period, and each hour of the day — each hora — is ruled by the next one along. A day holds 24 horas, and 24 ÷ 7 leaves 3, so tomorrow's first hora lands three places further round. Count in threes from the Sun: Sun → Moon → Mars → Mercury → Jupiter → Venus → Saturn. The weekday order is not arbitrary; it is that arithmetic.
diagrams.hora_cycle_label: The seven-graha hora cycle and the weekday order it generates
diagrams.manda_row_manda_note: orbit not centred on us — one wave per revolution
diagrams.manda_row_shighra_note: our own motion — this is where retrograde comes from
diagrams.manda_shighra_caption: A mean planet moves at a dead-constant rate around a circle: easy to compute and wrong on the sky. Two corrections repair it. The manda term accounts for the orbit not being centred on us, giving one wave per revolution; the shighra term accounts for our own orbital motion, and that is where the retrograde loop comes from. Applied in turn they leave the true position — the sphuta graha.
diagrams.manda_shighra_label: Manda and shighra corrections turning a mean planet into a true one
diagrams.moonrise_slip_caption: The Moon moves about 13° along its own orbit each day, so successive moonrises are about 24h 50m apart — always more than one civil day. The slip therefore accumulates until it steps clean over a day, which then has no moonrise at all. The reverse cannot happen: because the interval exceeds 24 hours, two moonrises never fall inside one day.
diagrams.moonrise_slip_label: Moonrise slips ~50 minutes a day — some days get two, some get none
diagrams.paksha_strip_caption: A lunation runs from new Moon through full and back to new. The waxing half is Shukla paksha and the waning half Krishna, fifteen tithis each — so the count runs 1 to 15 twice rather than 1 to 30 once, and the fifteenth takes a different name in each half: Purnima in the bright, Aunsi in the dark.
diagrams.paksha_strip_label: Shukla and Krishna paksha — the two halves of one lunation
diagrams.ray_angle_caption: The beam is the same width on both sides — the Sun is sending the same energy. Arriving steeply it concentrates on a short footprint; arriving at a slant it spreads across a long one, and the heat per square metre drops. This is what makes the seasons: the tilt changes the angle of the light through the year, not the distance.
diagrams.ray_angle_label: The same quantity of light arriving steeply and at a slant — spread over different areas
diagrams.retrograde_caption: Earth runs fast on the inner orbit, Mars slowly on the outer one. Follow the sightlines drawn from Earth to Mars at equal intervals: they sweep forward before the overtaking, backward through it, then forward again. The loop you see on the sky is made by those sightlines — Mars never actually moves backwards.
diagrams.retrograde_label: Retrograde motion — the sightline slides backwards as Earth overtakes
diagrams.retrograde_red_span: red span = retrograde — the sightline sliding back
diagrams.retrograde_star_backdrop: the fixed-star backdrop — the apparent path
diagrams.sidereal_day_caption: A mark on Earth starts lined up with both the Sun and a distant star. After one full rotation — 23h 56m — the mark points at the star again, because the star is far enough away that its direction has not changed. But Earth has moved about 1° along its orbit in that time, so it must turn that extra 1° to bring the Sun overhead again: roughly four minutes. The angle is exaggerated here to be visible.
diagrams.sidereal_day_label: Sidereal versus solar day — the four minutes added by 1° of orbital motion
diagrams.sidereal_panel_start: start — lined up on both Sun and star
diagrams.sidereal_scale_zero: sidereal — zero fixed against the stars (Baisakh 1)
diagrams.sidereal_star_direction: direction to the distant star — the same in both
diagrams.sunrise_sample_caption: A tithi can start and end at any hour, but a calendar needs one name per day. The rule is simply this: whichever tithi is running at the moment of sunrise is the tithi for that whole day. A tithi that ends before sunrise therefore never gets a day of its own. That one rule is what makes tithi local, because sunrise itself is local.
diagrams.sunrise_sample_label: The tithi running at sunrise is the tithi for the whole day
diagrams.tithi_zones_caption: The tithi ends at one absolute moment for the whole planet — 22:00 UTC here. All that differs is whether that moment falls before or after each place's sunrise. At Kathmandu it lands before dawn, so that day takes the next tithi; at Sydney it lands after, so the day keeps the earlier one. Both are right; the difference is in the sunrise rule, not in the astronomy.
diagrams.tithi_zones_label: One tithi boundary, two cities — which side of sunrise it falls on changes the answer
diagrams.tropical_scale_zero: tropical — zero at the spring equinox
diagrams.two_zeros_caption: Both zodiacs run 0° to 360° along the same ecliptic; all that differs is where the zero was put. The tropical zero is pinned to the spring equinox, the sidereal zero to the stars — and the second now sits about 24° behind the first. Everything else follows from that single offset: why the new year falls ~24 days after the equinox, why Makara Sankranti falls ~24 days after the winter solstice. It is one gap, read in different units.
diagrams.two_zeros_label: The tropical and sidereal zeros on one ruler, with the ~24° ayanamsha between them
diagrams.year_length_caption: The Julian rule calls a year 365.25 days when the true tropical year is 365.2422 — an overpayment of 0.0078 days annually. That amount, negligible over a lifetime, becomes a full day in 128 years and ten days by 1582. The Gregorian correction drops three leap days every four centuries, bringing the mean to 365.2425 — now it takes about 3,000 years to lose a day.
diagrams.year_length_label: Julian, Gregorian and true year lengths, and the error each accumulates

circumpolar.aria: The sky from Kathmandu's latitude — which stars never set and which never rise
circumpolar.caption: The celestial pole stands above the horizon by exactly the observer's latitude — 27.7° at Kathmandu — and every star circles that axis. A circle entirely above the horizon never sets; entirely below, it never rises. Kathmandu's limits are ±62.3°, and both the Saptarishi and Crux straddle them: the Dipper's tail dips below the horizon for part of the year, and the top of Crux does clear the southern horizon by a few degrees.

declination.aria: The Sun's declination through the year — zero at the equinoxes, extreme at the solstices
declination.caption: One curve, two different points — an equinox is where it crosses zero (the Sun on the celestial equator, day equal to night, north–south motion at its fastest); a solstice is where it turns (declination ±23.44°, the longest and shortest day). The B.S. months run underneath: none of the four lands on a month boundary, and over centuries they drift against them.

lunar_gap.aria: A lunar year falls 11 days short of a solar year — in three years the gap exceeds a month
lunar_gap.caption: Twelve lunar months make 354.4 days against a solar year of 365.24 — a shortfall of 10.87 days each year. It accumulates, and by the third year it reaches 32.6 days, longer than a lunar month itself. That is when an extra month is inserted to settle the account — the central mechanism of a lunisolar calendar.

month_lengths.aria: The lengths of the twelve Nepali months — short near perihelion, long near aphelion
month_lengths.caption: A solar month is not a count of days but 30° of the Sun's travel along the zodiac. Near perihelion (Poush–Magh) the Sun moves fastest, so those 30° take fewer days; near aphelion (Asar) it is slowest and the month stretches. That is why a Nepali month runs anywhere from 29 to 32 days.

orbit.caption_lead: The Sun sits at one focus — Earth orbits the true ellipse
orbit.caption_rest: Faster when near (perihelion / around winter), slower when far (aphelion / around summer) — which is why some months pass more quickly. Because the pole is tilted {{tilt}}°, solstices give long and short days while equinoxes give equal day and night.

ritu.aria: The six ṛtus, twelve months and four tropical markers on one wheel
ritu.caption: The ṛtus take their names from the months, but what makes a ṛtu is the Sun's north–south journey. Because those are two different frames, all four tropical markers (green = equinox, amber = solstice) fall inside a month rather than on its boundary — the summer solstice sits within Asar, not at the Jestha–Asar seam. Precession moves these markers 1° every 72 years, which is why the dependable reference for a ṛtu argument is Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana, not the months.

The orbit is an ellipse, not a circle: 0.983–1.017 AU (3.4%), and the Sun moves fastest when nearest — which is why a solar month runs 29 to 32 days. two_systems.model_caveat: These readings come from this view's own astronomical model — the sankranti and the tithi angle are right, but the sunrise rule that assigns a tithi to a civil day is not applied here. The daily panchanga remains authoritative.
two_systems.sidereal_vs_synodic: One lap — the sidereal month — is exactly 360° in 27.3 days. By then Earth has moved ~29° around the Sun, so the Moon is not beside the Sun again; it needs ~29° more to catch up. That is the synodic month: ~389° in 29.5 days. On the orbit, the first lap is the inner line and the overshoot is the outer green arc.
